PullRequest.Title: chat: use the remote connections toggle for Mission Control
PullRequest.Body:

## Summary

Use the existing **Allow Remote Connections** toggle for both Dev Tunnel sharing and Mission Control registration, instead of enabling Mission Control directly through a setting.

- Replace `chat.agentHost.experimentalMissionControl.enabled` with `chat.agentHost.remoteConnections`: `devTunnel` (default) or `missionControl`.
- Route the editor chat toolbar and Agents Window title-bar toggles to the selected backend. Selecting a backend alone never enables sharing; changing backends turns sharing off.
- Remember successful Mission Control opt-in locally, restore it after reload/restart, and withdraw access when disabled or AI features are hidden. Preserve authentication/account checks and cancellation guards.
- Update toggle progress, hover/ARIA state, accessibility help, documentation, and focused tests.

## How to Test

1. Open a desktop Agents Window or local Agent Host chat.
2. Confirm **Allow Remote Connections** retains its Dev Tunnel behavior by default.
3. Set `chat.agentHost.remoteConnections` to `missionControl`. Confirm this alone does not register the environment.
4. Enable the toggle and confirm registration/progress state; disable it to withdraw remote access.
5. Re-enable sharing, then change backends and confirm a fresh toggle opt-in is required.

Launched an isolated, GitHub-authenticated Agents Window and verified that the sharing toggle is visible. Live Mission Control registration was **not exercised**. The seeded profile reported remote-host connection and restored-session identity errors during launch. Full integration/smoke suites were not run.

(Written by Copilot)

RegressionFixes.Mechanism: The initial Agent Host connection event queued a second full Mission Control configure operation behind the first, duplicating authentication lookup, workspace-root preparation, management IPC, filesystem realpath work, GitHub identity resolution, and environment registration on every enabled cold startup.
RegressionFixes.Symptom: Mission Control opt-in or restored startup performed two serialized registration passes, extending readiness and duplicating IPC, filesystem, and network work.
RegressionFixes.FixedBehavior: The new sharing service ignores the Agent Host start event during the initial in-flight registration because _configured is false, then marks it configured only after configureMissionControl succeeds. A later real host restart still clears _configured and schedules exactly one replacement registration.
RegressionFixes.Evidence: In the base contribution, the initial _configure path called IAgentHostService.startAgentHost(), then awaited configureMissionControl over LocalAgentHostManagementConnection. That management channel cannot resolve until LocalAgentHostServiceClient reaches Connected; _handleConnectionState fires onAgentHostStart at that point. The base onAgentHostStart handler at line 100 unconditionally incremented the generation and scheduled another throttled _configure. Because the first _configure was active, Throttler retained one queued run; after the first IPC/network registration settled, that queued run repeated authentication.getSessions, workspace-root collection, startAgentHost, and configureMissionControl. The downstream MissionControlEnvironment registration resolves owner identity, realpaths roots, and performs GitHub registration/check-in network work. The PR's new line 106 gates the event on _configured, which remains false until the initial configureMissionControl has completed, while the added test still proves reconfiguration after a genuine later host restart.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore a remembered Mission Control sharing opt-in when a desktop workbench window reaches AfterRestored
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The sharing service reads application storage, then its zero-delay scheduler must obtain authentication sessions, start/connect the Agent Host, and complete Mission Control configuration before state becomes enabled. This work is on sharing-readiness rather than editor startup's restore barrier because both contributions run AfterRestored.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve authentication sessions with the required scopes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getSessions call per effective configure pass, independent per opted-in window
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed contribution performed the same lookup for every enabled configure pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must complete before the Agent Host can be configured

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start/connect the local Agent Host process
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Called once per effective configure pass; LocalAgentHostServiceClient deduplicates an already-created protocol client
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed contribution also called startAgentHost, but its start event then queued a duplicate full configure; this PR fixes that repeated pass.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The management channel cannot configure Mission Control until the host connection is available

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send Mission Control options to the Agent Host management channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per effective configure pass
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old enabled-setting path used the same management IPC, and initial host startup could cause it twice.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before sharing state becomes enabled

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Canonicalize each advertised workspace root with realpath
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One operation per local file workspace folder per configure pass
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same downstream configuration path canonicalized the same roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs transitively inside awaited Mission Control configuration

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve GitHub owner identity and register/check in the Mission Control environment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration sequence per effective configure pass; independent windows may contribute roots to the shared host
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The application-scoped boolean opt-in invoked the same sequence in each enabled window; the PR removes an initial duplicate sequence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before state changes from connecting to enabled

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One configuration pass per opted-in workbench window, with workspace-root preparation proportional to that window's local file-folder count. Multiple open windows execute independently against the shared Agent Host.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler collapses same-turn triggers and a per-window Throttler permits one active configure plus only the latest queued configure. Windows are not globally limited, matching the former application-scoped setting. The PR additionally removes the base path's guaranteed second serialized configure on initial Agent Host connection.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The remembered boolean is a warm application-storage read. Authentication session lookup may use provider caches, but Mission Control registration and workspace realpath/network work are not cached. Disabled or non-Mission-Control windows return before those boundaries; failures are not negatively cached and may retry only on later lifecycle events.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: contribution phase, event ordering, throttler semantics, management-channel readiness, and downstream filesystem/network operations were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual authentication cache hit rate, workspace-folder count, open-window count, and GitHub latency vary, but the call path and the removal of the duplicate initial pass are explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Remembered restoration preserves the former global opt-in's startup work, while the new _configured guard fixes a concrete duplicate-registration path; that fix was recorded separately.

Scenarios.Scenario: Enable or disable Allow Remote Connections with Mission Control selected
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Enablement first awaits Dev Tunnel shutdown, then authentication (and interactive sign-in only when needed), Agent Host startup, management IPC, and Mission Control registration. Disablement awaits withdrawal IPC; an offline heartbeat may be sent after local ingress is cleared.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop Dev Tunnel remote access before enabling Mission Control
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One stopTunnel call when Mission Control state is disabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The toggle previously controlled only Dev Tunnel; there was no backend handoff. The coordinator checks whether inactive mode is already satisfied, making the common no-tunnel case a bounded no-op without a CLI subprocess.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Obtain authentication sessions or create one interactively
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One getSessions and at most one createSession per explicit enable attempt
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old setting-based Mission Control enable path obtained sessions but did not interactively create one; the work moved to explicit user opt-in.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one actual start for an unstarted host; repeated method calls reuse the existing protocol client
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The setting-based enable path started the same host.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Register the environment or send an offline heartbeat during withdrawal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registration per successful enable and at most one offline heartbeat for an active registration on disable
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changing the old enable setting used the same registration and withdrawal path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Registration is awaited before enabled state; withdrawal clears ingress synchronously and the caller awaits queued cleanup

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the successful or cleared opt-in in application storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One small boolean write on success, explicit disable, or interactive failure
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Enablement was represented directly by the configuration setting rather than a separate storage key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Success persistence occurs after registration; disable stores before awaited withdrawal

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One user action and one local environment; registration root work scales with local workspace folders, not sessions or history items.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The sharing service serializes configure requests with a Throttler. Cancellation increments a generation so stale authentication/configuration results cannot publish enabled state. Withdrawal can run alongside an in-flight configure but generation fencing bounds the resulting calls to the in-flight operation plus one withdrawal.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Existing authentication sessions avoid createSession; a missing session on explicit enable invokes one interactive createSession. Successful opt-in is persisted only after registration succeeds; failed interactive registration clears it. No network registration result is cached beyond live configured state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all awaited boundaries and downstream no-op/serialization guards were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Tunnel coordinator IPC and authentication provider latency vary, but operation counts are fixed per click and subprocess creation is guarded downstream.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The newly introduced work is the bounded, intentional backend handoff required by the explicit toggle, and no collection fan-out or unbounded concurrency is added.

Scenarios.Scenario: Change the selected remote-connections backend while Dev Tunnel or Mission Control sharing is active or starting
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The configuration event immediately requests Dev Tunnel shutdown, clears Mission Control opt-in, and withdraws any active registration. These operations are not on typing/rendering/startup paths; they are triggered by an infrequent settings change.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Set Dev Tunnel remote access inactive
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per configuration event, plus one if a pending activation later emits active mode
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: There was no backend exclusivity setting, so this enforcement path did not exist.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the general UI critical path; asynchronous from the setting listener

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Stop active tunnel CLI and reconcile to inactive mode
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most the latest queued transition is reconciled; inactive satisfied state returns without spawning a CLI
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only explicit Dev Tunnel turn-off drove this transition.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Withdraw Mission Control configuration from the shared Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One meaningful withdrawal for an active registration; later disabled calls may cross IPC but downstream has no registered environment to heartbeat
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Disabling the old boolean setting performed the equivalent withdrawal.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Send an offline heartbeat for an actively registered environment
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one request because the first withdrawal clears the registered environment synchronously
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The old opt-in disable path sent the same offline heartbeat.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued host cleanup; remote ingress is cleared before the network request

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One backend-setting event, with a possible second tunnel-stop request if an in-flight Dev Tunnel activation later publishes active mode.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: TunnelProcessCoordinator generations and its promise queue coalesce/supersede competing tunnel transitions. Mission Control configure work is throttled, while generation checks prevent stale completion from re-enabling sharing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tunnel coordinator state makes an already-inactive stop a no-op before subprocess reconciliation. Mission Control retains live host state only while configured; the persisted opt-in is cleared on the first backend change.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: configuration listeners, mode events, coordinator generation checks, and withdrawal state clearing were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Whether a backend change races an activation and the tunnel process shutdown duration depend on user timing and platform.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The work is bounded to an explicit backend change, and downstream coalescing/no-op checks prevent repeated subprocess or network fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update toolbar/title-bar sharing visuals and accessibility help
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable/configuration/tunnel status events synchronously update a constant number of classes, ARIA attributes, hover text, and one context key. Accessibility help constructs one additional localized string only when the help view is requested.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant work per state/configuration event and per rendered toggle; no dependence on sessions, history, workspace size, or frame rate.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous observable reactions; no queued asynchronous work or expensive boundary is reached by the rendering helpers themselves.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: State is read directly from in-memory observables/configuration. Hover updates reuse the existing managed hover; no new retained collection or cache is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: added autoruns and update methods were inspected through their complete changed paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously rendered toggle instances is UI-layout dependent but normally one per relevant window and remains constant-scale.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding. The synchronous UI work is O(1), event-driven, and does not introduce layout reads, collection scans, or retained growth.

Scenarios.Scenario: Reconfigure or withdraw sharing after workspace-folder, authentication-session, entitlement, storage, or genuine Agent Host restart events
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Lifecycle events schedule a configure or immediate withdrawal. Configure re-reads sessions and may perform management IPC/network registration; withdrawal clears local ingress and may queue one offline heartbeat.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh authentication sessions and configure/withdraw the Agent Host
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active plus at most one coalesced configure per event burst per window; one immediate withdrawal on account loss/disable
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed contribution listened to the same workspace, authentication, entitlement, and host-start events and crossed the same boundaries; storage events replace global setting propagation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off interaction critical paths except that state remains connecting until replacement registration succeeds

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Re-register after a genuine host restart or relevant live-state change, or send one offline heartbeat on withdrawal
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one active and one latest queued registration per window burst; one offline heartbeat per live environment withdrawal
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same lifecycle events reconfigured the old setting-enabled service, but initial host startup also caused an unnecessary second registration; this PR removes that repeated work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines remote-sharing readiness, not local chat/session progress

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event burst per window; workspace-root work scales with local folder count and authentication filtering scales with the event's added/removed sessions.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: RunOnceScheduler coalesces same-turn schedules and Throttler collapses bursts to one active plus latest queued configure. Application-storage external changes can trigger independent work in each open window, as could the former application-scoped configuration opt-in. Genuine host restart schedules one replacement configure only after the service had been configured.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Live _configured state suppresses initial-start reconfiguration in the PR. Session IDs are retained only for the currently selected account and cleared on withdrawal. Failures are retried only on a later lifecycle event, not by an internal retry loop.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener ownership, disposal, generation fencing, scheduler/throttler behavior, and downstream host state were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Authentication providers may emit different event burst shapes and users may have multiple windows, but per-window coalescing and cross-window equivalence to the old global opt-in are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Lifecycle work remains bounded and coalesced, cleanup handles are disposed with the service, and the PR improves the initial-start case.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and every diff page. Traced startup restoration, explicit toggle, backend switching, UI updates, cross-window storage, and lifecycle reconfiguration through authentication, storage, Agent Host IPC/subprocess, filesystem, Dev Tunnel subprocess, and GitHub network boundaries. No diff-introduced actionable performance regression met the reporting threshold. Recorded the PR's high-confidence fix for duplicate initial Mission Control registration introduced by commit 431af7bbe286c90b2df828d495cf31e3e33f0fd7.
